author: Daniel Kornaś
text:
FlashVideo takes a staged route from a text prompt to 1080p video.

FlashVideo is a two-stage text-to-video generation repository for researchers and engineers experimenting with high-resolution video synthesis.

It helps you generate 1080p outputs by first producing 270p video, then enhancing it with a separate second-stage model.

Key features:
• Two-stage generation – separates prompt-to-270p synthesis from 270p-to-1080p enhancement.
• Released checkpoints – provides Stage I and Stage II weights plus 3D VAE setup instructions.
• Two inference paths – run prompts through a Jupyter notebook or a multi-GPU text-file script.
• Memory controls – adjust spatial and temporal VAE decoding slices for GPUs with less memory.
• Prompt guidance – includes a detailed example because both stages were trained with long prompts.

The code repository includes an Apache 2.0 license. The model weights use a separate CogVideoX license with registration requirements for commercial use.

author: Zarak Khan
text:
#Hiring #AIEngineer

Hiring AI Engineer 

Company: Lex and Link
Location: Bahria Town Phase 7, Rawalpindi (on-site preferred; hybrid negotiable)

Type: Full-time

Compensation: PKR 350,000–450,000/month, based on experience

About the Role
We're building an AI-powered engineering report pipeline for the US property insurance market—a system that takes property data, weather records, and roof imagery to produce citation-grounded, audit-ready observation reports for licensed Professional Engineers to review and seal.

This is not a "wrap an LLM around a prompt" project. The architecture deliberately limits the LLM to drafting, with determinations made by deterministic, unit-tested rules engines, citations resolved through retrieval against licensed references, and full provenance on every field. Defensibility is the product. If you've been burned by hallucinating chatbots in production and want to build something rigorous instead, this is that job.

You will be the first engineering hire, owning the technical build end to end while growing a small team as the project scales.

What You'll Build
A structured Fact Object pipeline: intake, geocoding, parcel/permit lookups, roof geometry ingestion, weather corroboration across APIs

A deterministic rules engine encoding published hail/wind damage thresholds (HAAG, ASTM, IBHS) with honest meets/below outputs

A RAG-constrained drafting engine: LLM prose generation with validators rejecting any number or citation not traceable to a verified source

A review console for licensed engineers: evidence linkage, edit logging, immutable audit trail, digital seal workflow
Integrations with third-party APIs: roof measurement (EagleView/HOVER), weather (NOAA, HailTrace), parcel data (Regrid/ATTOM), estimating (Xactimate)
Later: a computer vision model for roof damage detection and functional-vs-cosmetic classification trained on expert-adjudicated imagery

What We're Looking For
Must have:
5+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years shipping ML/AI systems to production
Strong backend skills (Python preferred)—design schemas, build services, write tests, and reason about data provenance
Hands-on experience with LLM applications: RAG pipelines, embeddings, retrieval quality, prompt and validation layers
Experience integrating third-party APIs behind clean interfaces
Judgment to know when not to use ML—comfortable building deterministic, auditable logic where correctness matters
Strong written English; you'll read US building codes and engineering standards

Nice to have:
Computer vision experience (object detection, image classification, model calibration)
Experience in insurance-tech, construction-tech, legal-tech, or another regulated/high-stakes domain
Familiarity with document processing, PDF generation, or audit/compliance tooling
Prior experience as a first or early engineering hire

To apply: Send your CV and written answer to careers@lexandlink.com with the subject line "AI Engineer".

author: Ritvvij Parrikh
text:
"We retrained and nothing moved." Said by a data scientist, it is a status update. Heard by non-technical management, it is a verdict.

A condition that was diagnosable and fixable gets read as terminal. And once you pull the plug on the feedback loop, recovery is brutal: the corpus now has a gap that cannot be backfilled at any price.

Dr. House would not tolerate this meeting. His rule: nobody announces the exotic diagnosis until the boring ones are excluded. Whiteboard first. Cheap tests first. The MRI never runs before blood pressure.

Part 9 of Techno-nomics applies that discipline to the most expensive sentence in applied ML. Six steps, ordered by cost, before anyone is allowed to say "plateaued." Because a plateau is a diagnosis of exclusion. And a verdict that skips the sequence is a guess with a budget attached.

author: Joel Suman
text:
🚀 Project #5 Completed | Heart Disease Prediction using Machine Learning

Over the past few weeks, I have been challenging myself to build one machine learning project after another. Today, I am excited to share my 5th project in my ML learning journey. This project focuses on Heart Disease Prediction using Logistic Regression, but my primary goal wasn't just building a classifier—it was learning how to build a professional, production-ready ML pipeline.

🔹 What I implemented:
- Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
- Data Cleaning
- Train-Test Split with Stratification
- Data Leakage Prevention
- ColumnTransformer
- Pipeline
- Missing Value Imputation
- Feature Scaling
- Ordinal & One-Hot Encoding
- Baseline Model (DummyClassifier)
- Hyperparameter Tuning with GridSearchCV
- Model Evaluation (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC)
- Confusion Matrix & Classification Report
- Model Interpretability using Logistic Regression Coefficients
- Saved the complete pipeline with Joblib
- Prediction on new unseen data

📌 Results:

One of my biggest takeaways from this project was realizing that a good machine learning model isn't judged by accuracy alone. Understanding evaluation metrics, preventing data leakage, and building reproducible pipelines are just as important as the model itself.

This project is another step toward becoming a better Machine Learning Engineer. Every project teaches me something new, and I am excited to keep learning and building. Feedback and suggestions are always welcome!

author: Sawan Mukhiya
text:
From May 6 to July 6, 2026, I had the opportunity to work as an AI/ML Engineering Intern at Camden Tools Ltd — and what a two months it has been 🎉

Working on a real, production-grade system from day one was humbling and exhilarating in equal measure. My core contribution was building a compliance-aware product classification pipeline — spanning four restricted inventory categories — that went all the way from raw, messy data to a live, decision-making system serving an actual business workflow.

Along the way, I got deep hands-on experience with things I once only read and prototyped about:
- Training and tuning XGBoost & LightGBM models with Optuna and grounding them in 384-dim SentenceTransformer embeddings — achieving F1 scores of 0.95, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.94 across the four classification domains (knives, fragile goods, liquids, and electrical plugs)
- Designing a FastAPI microservice with a three-zone probability decision system — items scoring within a calibrated uncertainty band around the threshold are flagged for human review, while high- and low-confidence predictions are auto-labeled — keeping reviewers focused only where the model genuinely wasn't sure
- Building a real-time Next.js Admin Dashboard wired into the ML backend — so reviewers could audit, resolve, and override model decisions with full auditability
- Dockerizing the entire ML + API stack for scalable production deployment

What I didn't expect was how much I'd grow in "thinking like an engineer" — balancing model performance with operational reliability, and learning that a great ML model is only as good as the system it lives inside.

I'm deeply grateful to the team at Camden Tools, Shreejal Maharjan for trusting me with real problems, real data, and real stakes. This experience has made me more certain than ever that my path lies in building intelligent, production-ready AI systems.

If you're working on ML infrastructure, AI-powered workflows, or just want to chat about the intersection of models and software engineering — I'd love to connect! 🤝
